subject: Renewal + Capacity Expansion: prebaked reserved nodes, throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@techforge.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: raj.patel@techforge.ai, procurement@techforge.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity ask (Q3)

Hi Markus —

Quick note as we start renewal planning: TechForge will be increasing inference volume for our live personalization pipeline starting July. Current Dedicated pool has worked well, but we expect a persistent +3x peak over current commit during 10-18 PST. Procurement is asking whether we can: 1) reserve additional GPUs for the 12-month contract, 2) get a throughput guarantee (tokens/sec) for our primary route, and 3) reduce scale-up lag for cold starts.

Attached is a short throughput spec (TechForge_RFP_ThroughputSpec.pdf) with expected qps/token distribution. Can you confirm feasibility and a ballpark for committed reserved nodes vs on-demand burst? Also curious about options for "prebaked" standby nodes that skip the normal boot/priming time.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if easier.

— Lina
Lina Gomez
Head of ML Platforms, TechForge AI

From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@techforge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity ask (Q3)

Lina —

Thanks for the spec, that helps a lot. Short answers up front: yes, we can add reserved capacity; yes, we can provide a route-level throughput SLO; and yes, we have a prebaked standby option (we call them "prebaked nodes") that reduces scale-up lag significantly compared to cold allocation.

High-level proposal for discussion:
- Add 24 reserved A40-equivalent GPUs for the 12-month renewal (monthly committed capacity).
- Provide a throughput SLO for your /generate route: 1,200 tokens/sec sustained (multi-instance aggregate) with a 99th-percentile latency target of 180ms for 512-token requests.
- Offer a prebaked standby pool sized at 4 instances (warmed runtime images + warmed KV cache for your model families) to reduce scale-up lag to <6s for the first request.
- Autoscale policy changes: min_replicas -> 6, max_replicas -> 40; scale-up step: 1-2 replicas per 10s, with an emergency burst to add up to 8 replicas if sustained queue depth exceeds threshold for 60s.

I'll loop in Marissa (renewals) and Karthik (ops) to pin pricing and the implementation playbook. Can we schedule a 30-min alignment early next week?

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@techforge.ai>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, procurement@techforge.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft renewal addendum + pricing range

Hi Lina / Raj —

Following Markus's notes, attaching a draft addendum (Renewal_Addendum_v2.docx) that formalizes the committed 24-GPU uplift, prebaked standby pool, and the throughput SLO. High-level pricing ranges:
- Reserved 24 GPUs: $48,000/month (list; we can discuss a committed discount)
- Prebaked standby pool (4 instances): $6,400/month (operational premium for prewarmed images + cache retention)
- Throughput SLO add-on (route-level SLA and runbook): $2,500/month

Operational notes we added to the doc:
- Scale-up lag objective for prebaked pool: median <3s, 95th <6s.
- Min/Max replica guardrails and safe-autoscale policy to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Billing: committed capacity billed monthly; burst usage billed at on-demand rates over commit.

Quick asks for the call: confirm peak windows, preferred billing term (12 vs 24 months), and whether TechForge needs an audit log export cadence for throughput verification.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@techforge.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, lina.gomez@techforge.ai, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@techforge.ai
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft renewal addendum + pricing range

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from procurement:
1) Can you add an objective measurement for the throughput SLO (we prefer tokens/sec aggregated by route per rolling 5-minute window) and an automated monthly credit calculation if SLO misses exceed 0.5% for the month?
2) For prebaked standby: does the cache retention imply we retain model-specific KV caches for the duration of the prebaked instance lifetime? What's the warm-cache hit-rate expectation after 24 hours idle?
3) We need a short implementation checklist for our ops team (networking/VPC peering, IAM roles for log export, and a dry-run date for cutover).

We can do the alignment call tomorrow at 09:00 PT.

— Raj
VP, Platform Engineering, TechForge AI

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@techforge.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, lina.gomez@techforge.ai
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, procurement@techforge.ai
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft renewal addendum + pricing range

Raj —

Answers inline to keep the thread tidy:

1) Throughput SLO measurement: we will instrument route-level aggregate tokens/sec using a 5-minute rolling window. If observed SLO misses >0.5% (per month) we propose a credit formula: credit = min(12.5% of monthly SLO add-on, prorated by miss percentage). We'll add exact metric ids into the addendum.

2) Prebaked standby cache retention: prebaked instances will preserve warmed model weights and KV caches for up to 72 hours of idle time. Expected cold-hit performance: after 24 hours idle, we expect a warm-cache hit-rate >= 78% for your primary model family (based on our benchmarks on similar token distributions). We'll include a cache-eviction policy in the ops doc.

3) Implementation checklist (high level):
- VPC peering and routes configured (target: 2 business days)
- IAM service account permissions and key exchange (1 business day)
- Dry-run: schedule a staged failover where prebaked pool handles 10% traffic for 24h (proposed: 2028-06-20)
- Post-cutover verification: throughput run at 60% peak for 30 minutes to verify SLO measurement and credits pipeline

I'll prepare the checklist as a short playbook and push a revision to the addendum. We're comfortable with the proposed min/max replica ranges but will parameterize them in the addendum so TechForge can adjust target min during overnight windows.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference
